advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] On trip, send the TRIP notification and persist state even when _apply partially fails (catch/collect failures rather than letting PolicyApplicationError skip notify and _save_state).
evidence: handler.py:571 `touched = _apply(attach=True)`
handler.py:444-446 `if failures:` ... `raise PolicyApplicationError(...)`
handler.py:576-586 the `if first_trip:` _notify block runs only AFTER _apply returns normally
handler.py:588 `_save_state(state)` is also skipped when _apply raises
advisory.finding: On a hard-cap TRIP, _apply(attach=True) raises PolicyApplicationError if ANY target fails to attach, and that exception propagates out of the handler BEFORE the TRIP notification is sent and before state['tripped_day'] / _save_state run. A trip that partially attaches the deny therefore produces no operator alert and no persisted state, even though enforcement partially engaged.
scenarios: Deny policy attaches to lmn-api but iam:AttachRolePolicy is throttled/denied for the Admin group during the trip

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Either consume state['tripped_day'] in the release/day-rollover logic or remove it to avoid implying it gates enforcement.
evidence: search for `tripped_day` returns only handler.py:573 (the write); no read site
handler.py:561 release guard uses any_attached/spend/signal_unavailable, not tripped_day
advisory.finding: state['tripped_day'] is written on every trip (handler.py:573) but is never read anywhere in the handler; the release decision keys only off `any_attached and spend < THRESHOLD_USD and not signal_unavailable`. The field is vestigial/misleading state — a reader would assume it gates the 00:00 UTC release.
scenarios: A maintainer edits release logic assuming tripped_day is consulted

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Use a stable budget name independent of the cap amount so cap changes update the budget in place rather than forcing replacement.
evidence: bedrock_spend_cap.tf `name = format("bedrock-daily-%s", var.bedrock_daily_cap_usd)`
README.md 'Change the cap: set `bedrock_daily_cap_usd` and apply.'
advisory.finding: The budget resource name embeds the dollar cap: name = format("bedrock-daily-%s", var.bedrock_daily_cap_usd). Because aws_budgets_budget name changes force resource replacement, raising/lowering the cap destroys and recreates the budget (and its notifications) rather than updating in place — contrary to the README's casual 'Change the cap: set bedrock_daily_cap_usd and apply'.
scenarios: Operator bumps bedrock_daily_cap_usd; terraform plans destroy+create on the budget and its alert notifications

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm blind fail-closed trip (metered+ce both unavailable) is intended, and consider requiring at least one live signal before a first-ever attach, or make the blind-trip notification explicit.
evidence: handler.py:511-513 `else: spend = THRESHOLD_USD; effective_source = 'metered_unavailable'`
handler.py:569 `elif spend >= THRESHOLD_USD and not attached:` — THRESHOLD>=THRESHOLD is true
handler.py:580-581 notification prints metered/ce '{metered_text}'/'{ce_text}' which are 'unavailable'
advisory.finding: When the fast metered signal is unavailable (metered is None) and CE is also unavailable/below threshold, spend defaults to THRESHOLD_USD, which satisfies `spend >= THRESHOLD_USD` and TRIPS the deny while the handler is effectively blind (effective_source='metered_unavailable'). This fail-closed trip fires with metered/ce both 'unavailable' in the notification and no real spend measurement.
scenarios: Both CloudWatch ListMetrics/GetMetricData and CE fail on a tick with no attachment yet

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add _seed_for tests for CacheReadInputTokenCount (base/10) and CacheWriteInputTokenCount (base*5/4) directions.
evidence: handler.py _seed_for: `if metric_name == "CacheReadInputTokenCount": return base / 10` and `if metric_name == "CacheWriteInputTokenCount": return base * 5 / 4`
Named violating input: `_seed_for("model", "CacheReadInputTokenCount")` with SEED_RATES={"model":{"input":10}} should return 1.0; no test asserts this.

ABSENCE: only test_seed_for_missing_output_rate_falls_back_to_observed_input and test_rate_for_unpriced_model_uses_fail_closed_fallback exercise _seed_for/_rate_for; no CacheRead/CacheWrite case exists in the test file.
advisory.finding: The seed-rate cache-token scaling branches in _seed_for are untested. handler.py adds `if metric_name == "CacheReadInputTokenCount": return base / 10` and `if metric_name == "CacheWriteInputTokenCount": return base * 5 / 4`, but the only _seed_for tests cover OutputTokenCount and the InputTokenCount fallback. A regression flipping these factors (or the corresponding TOKEN_METRICS multipliers 1/10 and 5/4) would mis-price cache tokens with no failing test.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a _rate_for test exercising RATE_OVERRIDES: a model id matching a pin needle resolves against the pinned usage-type fragment's observed rate.
evidence: handler.py: `for needle, fragment in RATE_OVERRIDES.items(): if needle in model_id: pin = _normalise(fragment)`
bedrock_spend_cap.tf: `bedrock_cap_rate_overrides = { "titan-embed-text" = "TitanEmbeddingV2-Text" }`
README.md: 'Without this pin, embedding tokens would be priced at the fail-closed fallback and trip the cap far too early.'

Named violating input: `_rate_for("amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0", "InputTokenCount", {"USE1-TitanEmbeddingV2-Text": <rate>})` — no test exercises RATE_OVERRIDES; every _rate_for test loads the default empty override map.
ABSENCE: search of the test file shows no reference to RATE_OVERRIDES, 'titan', or 'TitanEmbedding'.
blocking.finding: The RATE_OVERRIDES pin path in _rate_for is untested, despite being newly added and flagged load-bearing. handler.py adds `for needle, fragment in RATE_OVERRIDES.items(): if needle in model_id: pin = _normalise(fragment)`, and bedrock_spend_cap.tf sets bedrock_cap_rate_overrides = {"titan-embed-text" = "TitanEmbeddingV2-Text"}. No test drives _rate_for with a model id containing 'titan-embed-text' against rates keyed under a 'TitanEmbeddingV2-Text' usage type, so a regression that broke the pin (e.g. failing to normalise the fragment) would price embedding tokens at UNKNOWN_RATE_PER_1K and trip the cap far too early — exactly the failure the README says the pin prevents.
blocking.suggested_fix: Add a test that sets module.RATE_OVERRIDES = {"titan-embed-text": "TitanEmbeddingV2-Text"} and asserts _rate_for("amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0", "InputTokenCount", {"USE1-TitanEmbeddingV2-Text-input-tokens": rate}) returns rate rather than the fallback.

infra/terraform/variables.tf:1-5 variable "aws_region" { ... default = "us-east-1" } — Lambda/log-group/state-param inherit the provider region, so the hardcoded us-east-1 in the policy diverges the moment aws_region changes.
dropped.finding: The bedrock-spend-cap execution-role policy hardcodes the region 'us-east-1' in the CloudWatch Logs and SSM parameter resource ARNs, but the Lambda function, its log group, and the /bedrock-spend-cap/state parameter are all created in the provider's region (var.aws_region, default us-east-1). If aws_region is ever changed, the Lambda is deployed to the new region while its IAM grants still reference us-east-1, so log creation and state read/write are denied and enforcement silently stops.
dropped.suggested_fix: Replace the literal "us-east-1" in the Logs and State statement ARNs with var.aws_region (or a data.aws_region.current.name lookup), matching the region the Lambda/log group/state parameter are created in.
